mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the expected discount rate for future cash flows increases, reducing the present value of future equity returns and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically lower than in neutral regimes (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect size is smaller than estimated.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.5% over two consecutive months signals deflationary pressure, which lowers real discount rates and increases the present value of equity payoffs, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In deflationary regimes, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a neutral benchmark (mean of -0.1%) over the subsequent 6 months (Wilcoxon signed-rank p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs per month coincides with corporate optimism and reduces perceived risk, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 100,000 in a single month
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor expansion events, 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat on average (mean < 0.1%) with wide confidence intervals.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) surprises strongly upward for two consecutive months, it signals resilient supply-side momentum that boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In analogous past events, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the 95th percentile of baseline positive surprises (median > 0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 5% in the same month indicates weakening overall demand, which raises recession risk and is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥5% AND INDPRO decreases by ≥5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 10 such dual contraction events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than in single-signal contraction events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months reflects tight labor markets that can lead to wage inflation and higher cost of capital, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 5 such episodes, 60-day forward returns do not average below -0.5% (mean > -0.3%) with 95% CI not excluding zero.

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) falls by at least 1 percentage point in a month, it signals excess liquidity that typically flattens the real yield curve and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥1pp in a single month
failure_condition: In 8 such liquidity drawdowns, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than in liquidity-neutral periods (mean difference ≤ 0.05%, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months, following a period of sub-4% unemployment, is associated with reduced consumer and business confidence and predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises from <4% to >6% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market regime transition to stagnation
failure_condition: During analogous transitions, 5-day forward returns do not fall below -0.2% with 90% confidence intervals not including zero.
